name: Left communism in China
summary: Chinese left communism, in its best-documented form, is the ultra-left of the Cultural Revolution, which held that a new bureaucratic 'Red capitalist' class had taken over the party-state and had to be overthrown. It demanded that the old state machine be smashed and replaced by Paris Commune-type organs of mass power, with officials paid like ordinary people and recallable at any time. It rejected the Soviet road and the Revolutionary Committees, while remaining within a Maoist vocabulary.
scope: Represents the Cultural Revolution ultra-left of 1966-68, centered on Shengwulian in Hunan and Yang Xiguang's 'Whither China?' (January 1968), plus the Wikipedia account of the self-described 'ultra-left' and the 'bourgeois right' critique. Excludes Chinese Trotskyism, early Chinese anarchism, and post-Mao writers, which the sources I opened do not detail. Most statements outside class, state, revolution and religion are unaddressed in these texts and are answered at low confidence.

sources.title: Whither China?
sources.author: Yang Xiguang (Yi-bing) for Shengwulian of Hunan
sources.usedFor: Smashing the state machine, Commune-type power, recall and equal pay for cadres, armed revolution, Red capitalist class, warning against the Soviet road, hostility to religion.

sources.title: Left communism in China
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition of the ultra-left, bourgeois right under socialism, wage system, Shanghai commune and strike.

sources.title: Shengwulian
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Shengwulian's Commune model, new bureaucratic bourgeoisie, opposition to revolutionary committees, suppression.

sources.title: Introduction to Whither China? (International Socialism)
sources.author: Tony Cliff
sources.usedFor: Reading of the text as anti state-capitalist, Commune state with standing army abolished.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed; an egalitarian anti-bureaucratic socialism would favor guaranteed public services, but Whither China? never addresses healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is not addressed as a minimum-wage question; ultra-leftists attacked the eight-grade wage system itself and the Shanghai strikers' demands were called economistic, so adherents are not clearly for reform-style wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ultra-left saw money exchange and distribution by work as persisting bourgeois right to be restricted, so markets allocating resources is alien to it.

public-ownership.rationale: Assumes social ownership of industry as the socialist baseline, but its demand is for who controls it (the masses, not bureaucrats), so formal public ownership alone is not endorsed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Attacks the high salaries and privileges of the Red capitalist class; tax policy as such is not discussed, so this is inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Adherents organized as independent rebel groups and Shanghai workers struck against official bodies; there is no stated view of unions as institutions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Calls for the redistribution of assets and power and for smashing the old order; private property as an overriding right is the opposite of this program.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations as such are not an issue in a state-owned economy; the target is the bureaucratic ruling class, so regulation is not a natural frame.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts are not discussed; a movement defending the masses against a privileged bureaucracy would oppose cuts, though it distrusts state handouts as a solution.

worker-ownership.rationale: Wanted mass democratic control over production through Commune-type power, which implies workers collectively running enterprises, though specifics are scarce.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; Shengwulian was denounced and crushed by the security apparatus, so its adherents would be wary of state surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source states any ultra-left position on drug policy, and nothing in its class-power focus points either way.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; a group whose speech was suppressed by the state would distrust state-run speech limits, though it is not libertarian on principle.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposed the dictatorship of the bureaucracy and demanded cadres be dismissed at any time by the masses, rejecting rule by a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Wanted the old state smashed but replaced by a Commune-type state and an armed mass dictatorship, so not stateless but not accepting the state either.

limit-guns.rationale: Complained that workers were disarmed and endorsed arming the left and an armed citizenry, so strict gun limits cut against it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Says the army and police became tools suppressing the revolution and demands the standing army be abolished or radically changed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist critique of commodification and exploitation suggests mild opposition to treating sex as a market, inferred only.

decide-locally.rationale: The Commune model implies power from below, though it also calls for a centralized revolution; inferred from the People's Commune of China idea.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is absent from the ultra-left texts; they endorse force against the bureaucratic class but say nothing about prison aims.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed; the text's mockery of inherited belief and its drive to break old hierarchies suggest skepticism of traditional family as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Cultural Revolution ultra-left texts do not address sexuality, and Maoist-era China gives no guide to an adherent's view.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in sources; inferred from a Marxist egalitarian orientation rather than any stated ultra-left position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Whither China? speaks of the powerful rule of religious thought and mocks idol worship, in line with Marxist secularism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a theme in the Chinese ultra-left, which focused on class.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed in any source I opened, so no inference is safe.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Aimed at a revolutionary break with the old order and disliked inherited ideas; culture preservation is not among its concerns.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects peaceful transition and reformism, insisting revolution is one class overthrowing another by force and that the state machine be smashed utterly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; class internationalism makes restricting immigration unlikely to be its stance.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalist but views imperialism as failing; no stated role for international bodies such as the UN, so mild inference.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; its hostility to money exchange and bourgeois right implies skepticism that trade benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: It is class-based and internationalist in outlook, and ignores nationalism, though it uses the term People's Commune of China.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; anti-imperialism suggests suspicion of foreign military interventions justified by rights.

open-borders.rationale: Not discussed; proletarian internationalism points toward eventual open borders, but sources are silent.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the Maoist-era framework treated production growth as a material basis for socialism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1967-68 movement, with nothing in its program to infer from.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; its analysis puts social class power, not technology, at the root of problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic to its sources, and no stance follows from its class politics.

revolution-justified.rationale: Whither China? endorses armed seizure of power and says the bureaucratic dictatorship must be overthrown by force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Calls for mass supervision of cadres and for senior cadres to step aside, rejecting rule by officials or experts above the masses.

central-planning.rationale: Planning is not discussed; the group criticizes bureaucratic control of the economy, which implies skepticism of bureaucratic planning but not rejection of planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Seen as persisting bourgeois right to be restricted, so market exchange even by public enterprises is disfavored, though not explicitly addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single-tax reform fits poorly with a program of overthrowing the state and redistributing assets and power.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Opposes privilege passing to the new ruling class; inheritance taxation is not specifically discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; its opposition to wage hierarchy might favor equal income, but it also stressed control over production rather than transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not part of its domestic-focused program.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The bureaucratic state is the enemy class; adherents would not entrust investment to it without mass control.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wants collective control, not small-owner capitalism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ultra-leftists treated money exchange and the eight-grade wage system as persisting bourgeois right, though abolition is inferred rather than demanded explicitly.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the sources.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Shanghai ultra-left opposed absorption of independent worker demands into state-sanctioned bodies, rejecting top-down class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Calls for a revolutionary party of the advanced proletariat but doubts the party under its current leadership and demands mass control over it; not support for single-party rule by an elite.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Radical communism rejects hereditary rule, and the text condemns feudalism.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls the goal mass dictatorship rather than democracy, but wants mass democratic control by Commune-type power; it rejects liberal democracy while demanding popular rule.

direct-votes.rationale: Commune-type mass power and dismissal of cadres by the masses point to direct popular decision-making, though referendums are not mentioned.

workers-councils.rationale: Calls for political organs of the Paris Commune type in place of the existing state, and compares Shengwulian to the soviets of 1917.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nationalities and secession are absent from the ultra-left texts I read.

natural-rulers.rationale: Directly opposes a ruling class of cadres and demands equal treatment with the masses.

political-violence-never.rationale: Endorses armed mass dictatorship and force to overthrow the bureaucratic dictatorship.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; not a militarist outlook, though accepts armed struggle.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular and hostile to religious thought; strict separation is not discussed, so inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mocks religious thought; a Marxist movement rejects scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Opposes private power; rejects handing coercion to private firms by inference from Commune politics.

military-superiority.rationale: Wants the army to be a big school and united with the people; military superiority as a goal is not addressed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Class-based, not ethnic; not addressed directly.

class-struggle-history.rationale: States that revolution is one class overthrowing another and that struggle continues against a new Red capitalist class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Demands cadres receive the same treatment as ordinary people and attacks high salaries and privileges.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not relevant to the sources, which concern class conflict among Han-majority Chinese cadres and masses.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; anti-imperialist but no source states a claim on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Class internationalism, not civilizational blocs; not addressed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Opposes bourgeois right and material privilege; a communist ethic of collective struggle.

duties-before-rights.rationale: It demands democratic rights and control for the masses over officials; subordinating rights to duties echoes bureaucratic demands for obedience.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy does not appear in Cultural Revolution ultra-left writing, and a Marxist outlook does not settle it.

limit-population.rationale: Demographic policy is not addressed in the sources, and nothing in a class analysis points either way.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: It treats the problem as bureaucratic class rule, not industry as such, so wholesale condemnation of industrial civilization is unlikely.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources never discuss technological change or institutional disruption by technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1960s movement; no principle in its texts bears on bodily enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Opposes rule by officials rather than masses; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic for 1967-68; its suppression by the state suggests sympathy but no source speaks to it.

restore-past-order.rationale: It seeks continuous revolution and condemns the restoration of old hierarchies via the revolutionary committees.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Strongly ideological; pragmatic evaluation of policies is not a stated principle.

direct-action.rationale: Rebel groups acted outside official channels, demanding armed seizure of power and mass action; elections are not discussed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not stated; also endorses violence to overthrow bureaucrats while aiming at a Commune.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxist and productivist; no primitivist current.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Aims to remove the distinction between cadres and masses; wider abolition is inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Sees distribution by work and the wage grades as bourgeois right to be restricted, pointing toward distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Critiques money exchange and bourgeois right persisting under socialism, implying production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Argues the Red capitalist class lives by exploiting the masses through privilege; classic profit theory is not detailed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Calls for an armed mass dictatorship over the bureaucratic class.

collective-farming.rationale: Supports a peasant movement but gives no stated view on collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Treats imperialism as going downhill toward debacle; war causation not argued.

taxation-theft.rationale: Marxist; the state is to be replaced, not tax per se rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: It endorses armed dictatorship over the bureaucratic class, which goes beyond restricting only harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Class and mass framing rather than an individual-rights framework, though not stated.

conscription.rationale: Calls for abolishing the standing army and arming the people.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emphasizes mass voice and control over leaders.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects hierarchy and bureaucracy and wants officials paid like the masses; the customer-citizen model is a market logic it opposes.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material conditions and power over production are central; not explicitly argued.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a theme; real power is attributed to the bureaucratic ruling class.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxist egalitarian outlook rejects genetic hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects hierarchical cooptation in favor of Commune-type power from below with recall.

total-state.rationale: Calls for abolishing bureaucratic organs and smashing the state machine.

national-rebirth.rationale: A class movement not centered on national decadence; it speaks of revolution against a bureaucratic class.

territorial-expansion.rationale: It denounces imperialism, and a proletarian-internationalist group would not endorse expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Opposes cadre privilege and personal loyalty hierarchies.

bound-labor.rationale: Calls the new order feudal-like and supports peasant movements.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The ultra-left texts are political, not epistemological, and Marxists differ on whether knowledge is class-bound.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral philosophy is not discussed; Marxism has been read both ways.

single-common-good.rationale: Class conflict rather than a common good is its premise, but a single reasoned common good is not discussed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Chinese ultra-left sources never mention Zionism or Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora questions do not appear in the sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a theme in the ultra-left texts.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mass democratic control over production through Commune power.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not discussed; market allocation of schooling contradicts its egalitarian orientation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic stabilization is not discussed in the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; liberal framing of economic freedom as precondition of political freedom is alien to it.

rule-by-example.rationale: Demands recall and mass control rather than trusting rulers' morals.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; focuses on class rather than national questions.

force-without-un.rationale: It says nothing about international law or Security Council authorization.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Hostile to religious thought but no stated epistemology.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist and class-based outlook disfavors citizenship-based entitlement.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; disciplining the poor contradicts its stance for the masses.

class-collaboration.rationale: Insists on class struggle against the Red capitalist class and rejects reformist compromise.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; the Cultural Revolution context involved attacks on old culture but the ultra-left sources say nothing here.

dominated-front.rationale: Whither China? invokes anti-imperialism as past struggle but proposes no front of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Its project is class-based revolution against a domestic ruling class, with proletarian internationalism as background, not nationally bounded labor.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian orientation suggests opposition.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not discussed; its critique of money exchange is about wage and bourgeois right, not interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: A Marxist egalitarian movement opposed to privilege would reject legal racial separation, though the sources never mention it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Calls the existing state an apparatus of a ruling class to be smashed and replaced.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not discussed; productivist Maoism would not oppose it but nothing is stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; a class-internationalist movement would not demand cultural assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theories about immigration contradict its class analysis of power, though the topic is absent from the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary electoral systems are not its concern.

national-mission.rationale: It denounces imperialism and treats the Soviet model as a warning; spreading one's own state form is not its stance.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources I read do not discuss gender hierarchy, so I cannot infer a position.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes cadres as a privileged Red capitalist class living on high salaries and exploitation.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts the egalitarian, materialist outlook of a communist movement, though not discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Complains of repression of the left; accountability inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Whither China? demands a sweeping social revolution and an armed mass dictatorship, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts egalitarian internationalism; the sources never raise it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Its demand that officials receive the same treatment as masses rests on equality of persons.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Whither China? warns against the Soviet road, but I found no passage on whether socialism can last in one country.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is outside the sources' focus on class conflict inside China.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions do not appear in the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Hostile to religious thought, but state restriction of religious choice is not discussed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious-based bans are alien to its hostility to religious thought.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hostile to religious thought, so likely supports secular schools, inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Demands smashing the state, though does not discuss the encirclement doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cadres removable at the masses' demand, but consent theory is not framed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are not discussed.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts class solidarity and Marxist egalitarianism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Whither China? says the bureaucratic dictatorship must be overthrown by force and endorses armed seizure of power.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Its theory is class struggle and mass solidarity, not competition between individuals or peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Group was itself suppressed; inferred opposition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Opposes bureaucratic domination, though this republican concept is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Wants unified Commune-type power rather than checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Calls for a revolutionary party of advanced proletarians but distrusts the existing party and favors mass initiative; Cliff also notes Mao's party attacked as privileged class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Aims for the masses against a privileged class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not in the sources; privatization of public housing is at odds with its anti-property stance but no source says so.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Shanghai strikers' demands were suppressed as economistic; adherents oppose such restrictions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: It locates oppression in the Red capitalist class, not demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Class-internationalist; the claim is foreign to its framework.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; recall and Commune power are its stated tools.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Victims of repression; but endorses revolutionary dictatorship.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian orientation suggests support.

party-controls-media.rationale: Group was denounced and suppressed; wanted mass voice.

party-commands-army.rationale: Wanted the army united with the masses and its tool role ended.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist orientation suggests opposition.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cadres would receive the same treatment as the masses; Commune precedent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: It wants a revolutionary party of advanced elements but distrusts the existing party and favors mass initiative.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; EU-style supranational unions are capitalist projects.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Opposes concentration of command in one person; wants armed masses and abolition of standing army.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religious hierarchy is not discussed; a movement mocking religious thought and favoring recallable authority would disfavor bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hostile to religious thought and rule by unelected authorities.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed in its Chinese setting; revolutionary defeatism toward the bureaucratic state is consistent with its stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; its members were suppressed and denounced, so state moral censorship is unlikely favored.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Cadres dismissable by the masses at any time.

recall-officials.rationale: New cadres may be dismissed or changed at any time according to the masses' demands.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not addressed, and its anti-imperialism points in different directions.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; homeownership for everyone is a petty-bourgeois aim.

people-in-arms.rationale: Backs arming the left and workers' militias and abolishing the standing army in favor of armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: It backs the peasant movement but gives no moral praise of rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not a theme of the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Its authors were young intellectuals and students, so it would not endorse this broad distrust.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian internationalism suggests agreement.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; it endorses armed force against class enemies but says nothing about judicial executions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular egalitarian orientation suggests mild support.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The text mocks religious thought, so religious doctrine in science teaching would be rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Sexual morality is not discussed in the ultra-left texts.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; class internationalism disfavors ancestry-based membership.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian orientation suggests mild support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Hostile to religious thought, so special exemptions for religion are unlikely to be supported, inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about social conformity is outside the ultra-left texts.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; anti-imperialist orientation suggests support.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Struggle against imperialism, bureaucratic capitalism, and feudalism linked; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: It calls for smashing the old state and Commune-type organs; an elected constituent assembly is not its mechanism.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: It demands mass democratic control and attacks bureaucratic dictatorship; trading freedom for growth is the bureaucracy's logic.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; its anti-imperialism leaves aid-as-duty unclear.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is not discussed in the sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: It wants Commune power and recallable cadres rather than a head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; insulating technocrats from popular control conflicts with its mass control demand.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; it favors abolishing private ownership rather than conditioning it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cliff reads the group as treating bureaucratic state capitalism as a global target, and Whither China? warns against the Soviet road, though it does not use the exact label for the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not part of the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliance doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law is not discussed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hostile to religion but proposed smashing the state itself.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: It wants no head-of-state institution; not addressed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity and secession are not addressed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Whither China? demands cadres be recallable and equal to the masses, and mocks idol worship.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; flat taxes contradict its egalitarian orientation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism is its framework, though not stated on this point.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Cadres are to be dismissable at any time by the masses, so no ruler stands above accountability.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not discussed; no principle in its texts bears on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rejects rule by the few; wants Commune power by the masses.

leader-cult.rationale: Criticizes Mao for opposing the Commune; not a personality cult line.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Argues a new Red capitalist class arose in socialist China and must be overthrown.

land-redistribution.rationale: Backs a peasant movement and redistribution of assets.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist orientation suggests support.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hostile to religious coercion; not discussed directly.

women-must-cover.rationale: Its mockery of religious thought implies opposition to religious law compelling women's dress, inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; class rather than kinship is its organizing principle.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The sources are silent on minority self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy questions of this kind do not appear in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist class analysis of the new bureaucratic bourgeoisie.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is irrelevant to its focus on bureaucratic state power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review is outside its program, which wants the old state machinery smashed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are not discussed in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; closed imperial blocs contradict its anti-imperialism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements are not part of the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ultra-left critique of bourgeois right might favor, but not stated.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution through mass movement rather than a small cell; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Attacks the privileges of the Red capitalist class and demands cadres live on the same terms as the masses, which extends naturally to hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: No source on how the ultra-left would want history taught; its class framing is neither nation-centered nor explicitly against it.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The text frames imperialism as a system heading for collapse, so rule by a 'more advanced' society over others would be rejected as imperialist.

patriotic-education.rationale: The ultra-left was class-based and hostile to state-run ideology, but patriotic schooling is not discussed in these sources.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions are not a topic in China's Cultural Revolution ultra-left, so no position can be documented.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed; the ultra-left questioned money exchange itself rather than who issues it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whither China? says imperialism is going downhill toward its debacle, which implies capitalism cannot avoid general crisis.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-imperialist; cultivating influence over former possessions is imperialism by another name for this outlook.

delink-world-market.rationale: The text names imperialism as an enemy but proposes no policy on trade ties, so this stays neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: No documented view on rich-country workers; a Chinese ultra-left focused on its domestic bureaucracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: An egalitarian movement against privilege would reject a right of owners to exclude people, though the topic is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights entrenchment is not addressed; the text rejects the existing state machinery rather than proposing a charter.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not a concern of the sources, which deal with domestic class conflict.

elective-rulers.rationale: Commune-type power with cadres dismissable at the masses' demand implies elected, recallable officials, though hereditary monarchy is not itself discussed.

minority-veto.rationale: Wanted decisive revolutionary action by the masses and mass dictatorship, not consensus procedure where one dissenter blocks.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Endorses force against a bureaucratic ruling class, but the constitutional-law framing is foreign to it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Wanted Commune-type organs replacing the state machine, not parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the ultra-left texts.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the ultra-left texts.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The ultra-left treated privilege as the mark of an exploiting class and demanded abolition, not benevolent duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Its whole project was mass political action, the revolutionary seizure of power from the bureaucracy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources focus on bureaucratic power, not cultural reproduction of domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The text stresses force and mass dictatorship rather than analyzing how rulers win consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mentions imperialism as an old enemy but offers no world-system analysis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalist class politics but not specifically addressed.

party-own-road.rationale: The text criticizes drift toward the Soviet road, but no source on whether parties should choose their own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy is outside what the sources say, though Maoist self-reliance was in the background.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims are not part of its program; class struggle is.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional design for democracies is not addressed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: It considers the bureaucratic state a class dictatorship to overthrow but would reject equating communism with fascism as Marxists.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: US history is outside the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not addressed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not discuss gender inequality.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources do not discuss domestic violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: It claimed the Paris Commune model as of general validity.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Says the army became a tool for suppressing revolution and calls for it to change radically; the group opposes a guardian army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labor is not discussed in the ultra-left texts I found.

filial-duty.rationale: Family ethics are not discussed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Wants officials removable by the masses; expert-selected officialdom is the bureaucracy it attacks.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not a question the sources raise; bureaucratic state ownership is itself the ultra-left's target.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian secular orientation.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cadres in the Commune order may be dismissed or changed at any time in accordance with the masses' demands.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private accounts are not discussed; contradicts egalitarian orientation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land question is not discussed beyond supporting peasant movement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary procedure is not part of its program of replacing the state with Commune organs.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership rules for foreigners are not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law doctrine is not discussed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumption culture is not discussed; its critique targets officials' privileges.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Foreign policy tools are not discussed in the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Cliff links the group against both capitalist and state-capitalist bureaucracy; the Soviet-style intervention into allies is the Soviet road it warns against.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is not relevant to its domestic bureaucratic target.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The sources do not discuss NGOs or foreign funding.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local housing regulation is not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its orientation toward the masses.

democratic-peace.rationale: Treats imperialism as the world order; democratic-peace theory is a liberal thesis it would not hold.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Calls for overthrowing the existing state with force, suggesting no general duty to obey its law.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not set out a doctrine on sovereignty and intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed; the Shanghai strikers' demands were suppressed by official worker organizations.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy against a minority is incompatible with Marxist class analysis.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in the sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The group demanded mass supervision of officials, which presupposes access to information.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not part of its program.

informal-organisation.rationale: It organized as loose alliances of rebel groups, but no source states a preference for small trust-based groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Legal hierarchy between national and international law is not discussed.

religious-nation.rationale: The text mocks religious thought; a Marxist group would reject religion as a national basis.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposes hierarchy and imperialism; also warns against copying the Soviet model.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist distinction between personal belongings and means of production; not discussed explicitly.

defeat-communism.rationale: The group is communist; hostility to this goal is built in.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; private providers fit poorly with its orientation.

religion-illusion.rationale: The text derides religious thought and belief in idols, in the Marxist tradition.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: It deals with Red capitalists in China; historical role of capitalism is not discussed.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist outlook; not discussed in these sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though Marxist tradition often supports it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaties are outside the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Commune model is a mass state, not a network of small communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-directed settlement of majorities contradicts class internationalism, inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The group is communist and claims the true socialist goal; third ways are rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Class internationalism disfavors ethnic and religious claims to land, but the sources do not discuss them.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts leftist historical outlook; not directly discussed.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The ultra-left sources do not discuss sexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The group was itself suppressed; though advocating dictatorship over class enemies.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hostile to religion; the text mocks religious thought.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialist: calls imperialism a system going downhill.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable; religious obligation conflicts with its Marxism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious criteria for legitimacy conflict with its Marxism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Shengwulian drew on the Paris Commune for mass democratic control by ordinary people in work and politics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The sources focus on class domination by bureaucrats without discussing intersecting oppressions.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics are not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It defined itself as further left than the Maoist leadership; left and right are central.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not used by the sources, but the critique of bureaucratic domination over producers fits it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A Marxist internationalist view of class does not hold that a religion is incompatible with a civilization, inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mocks religious thought; authority comes from the masses.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress rules in state institutions are not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Treats distribution by work and money exchange as bourgeois right to be restricted.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cliff notes the group proposes a Paris Commune type of state with the standing army abolished.

rich-first.rationale: Attacks bureaucrats' privileged position; rejects inequality that goes first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Its objection to the Soviet road does not state a neutrality policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rejects privilege and demands recall of cadres by the masses.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit schemes are not in its program.

property-franchise.rationale: Mass democratic power; the opposite of a property-based franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism does not appear in the sources.

reification.rationale: The sources do not use Lukacs-style theory, though Marxist critique of commodity relations overlaps.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Believed power lies with a ruling class; the argument about press ownership is not explicit.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law doctrine is not discussed; it demanded smashing the existing state machinery.

racial-franchise.rationale: A communist movement for mass democratic power would reject race-limited voting, though not discussed.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; its demand for mass supervision of cadres suggests sympathy but no source speaks to it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hostile to religion's control over private life.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Scapegoating a minority contradicts class solidarity, inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition is not discussed; its stated mechanism is Commune organs and recall.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed beyond mockery of religious thought.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Critique of privilege and concentration of power in the Red capitalist class.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Sexuality and military service are not discussed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mocks religion, but promoting atheism through the state is unaddressed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Wanted the existing state apparatus smashed; the replacement of police is not described.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are not discussed; they sit poorly with its class framework.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not discussed; collective emancipation rather than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Cadres are recallable, but fixed term limits are not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: The group wants cadres recallable by the masses, but no source supports individual proxy delegation of votes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk policy is anachronistic for its sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious institutions are not discussed beyond hostility to religious thought.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist egalitarianism suggests agreement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; proletarian internationalism suggests agreement.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not discussed; its egalitarian outlook suggests support.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rebel Red Guards were youth but organized outside official discipline.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not discussed in the ultra-left texts.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Historical atrocities recognition is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Its critique concerns privilege; but distribution by work was itself called bourgeois right.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Endorses armed struggle and armed mass dictatorship.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Its class framing and break with old order suggest little interest in national continuity.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Martyr cults for the nation are not discussed.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Class struggle, not spiritual struggle; religion mocked.

culture-before-state.rationale: Priority is political power seizure, state smashed first.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is not discussed beyond mockery of religion.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not discussed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic nationalism contradicts class internationalism, inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ethnic territorial units are not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Shanghai workers sought independent demands against official absorption; no stated union policy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Argues that China under revolutionary committees was not socialist because power lay with the bureaucrats, not the masses.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not discussed; its anti-private-property orientation suggests support.

second-chamber.rationale: The Commune model unifies power, not a bicameral system.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership as a model is not discussed; it wanted a national Commune.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Commune concept resembles delegated administration but the text calls for a People's Commune of China as a whole.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; it criticized the wage grading system itself.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension research is absent from the sources and anachronistic for 1967-68.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital payment privacy is anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on traceability of money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Internet anonymity is anachronistic for a 1968 text, so no position can be documented.

person-over-state.rationale: Personalist philosophy is not in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Class, not race, is the organizing principle.

racial-pride.rationale: Race is not discussed in the sources.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Military doctrine is not discussed; it endorsed internal armed struggle.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates contradict its class-based mass democracy, inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; egalitarian orientation suggests support.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist traditions often favored it, but the sources are silent.

capital-controls.rationale: Cross-border capital flows are not discussed in the sources, which concern domestic class power.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Whither China? demands the old state machine be smashed utterly and replaced by Commune-type organs, a position no current statement captures.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Shengwulian and similar groups looked to armed mass organisations and the Paris Commune model, so a state-only monopoly on arms sits badly with them (inferred).

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Internationalist and anti-bureaucratic, but the Maoist framework also endorsed revolutionary wars, so this is not clearly settled.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage bargaining was dismissed as economism, and the ultra-left aimed to abolish the wage hierarchy rather than negotiate within it (inferred).

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Topping up wages through the state is a reformist measure that the ultra-left, who sought to overthrow the new bureaucratic class, would not endorse (inferred).

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal fiscal limits are a bureaucratic constraint that does not fit a Commune-style order; not addressed (inferred).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialist, but the texts look to revolution rather than reform of international economic rules.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Whither China? sets out a fixed Commune-type model for the whole country, so an open-ended pluralism of systems is not its aim (inferred).

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; pricing nature as capital is at odds with an anti-capitalist programme (inferred).

sacred-nation.rationale: The texts put class and world revolution before the nation, though they stay within a Chinese Maoist vocabulary (inferred).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; there was no student loan system in the period and the ultra-left's concerns lay elsewhere.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the analysis is of a bureaucratic class rather than regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The texts follow Marxist class analysis, and the Cultural Revolution stressed remaking people, which cuts against a fixed human nature (inferred).

public-service-media.rationale: The ultra-left demanded mass control of media from below and attacked party-controlled media, but not a state-funded independent public broadcaster (inferred).

religions-one-truth.rationale: A Marxist materialist outlook rejects religious truth claims, though Whither China? does not discuss it; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: An egalitarian, anti-bureaucratic socialism would back protecting peasants from markets and moneylenders; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Whither China? does not address nuclear weapons; adherents' position unknown.

workers-own-party.rationale: It wanted new organs of mass power outside the bureaucratic party-state, which implies independent working-class organisation; inferred from Whither China?.

ban-fgm.rationale: An egalitarian socialism opposes harmful practices against women; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal rights for women are part of the Maoist egalitarian vocabulary it stayed within; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the sources read.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: It sought mass political organs, not private tort remedies; inferred from its anti-market socialism.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: It demanded smashing the old order and replacing it with Commune-type organs elected by the masses, leaving no room for hereditary or customary authority; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Its Commune model has officials recallable and accountable to the masses, against fixed rules removing discretion from judges; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; immigration was not an issue in the texts.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Whither China? does not discuss union membership rules; the demand for workers' own organs of power does not settle compulsory versus voluntary dues.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; Commune-style elections are demanded but identification rules for voting are unaddressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Commune model of a state that does not privilege any institution; the texts do not address interpretations within a religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Whither China? demands real mass power through Commune-type organs and recallable officials, and says elections held under a new privileged class do not amount to popular rule.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; sexual morality was not a topic of the ultra-left texts.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the demand for mass democratic control and freedom of expression against the state machine; the issue is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; a plan to merge welfare into one cash payment sits oddly with an egalitarian anti-bureaucratic socialism seeking collective control of production.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian call for Commune-style democracy open to all; women's rights are not specifically discussed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist tradition tends to trace women's oppression to class society rather than to religion, and the sources do not say more.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist class framing of the ultra-left, which treats social divisions as products of class power; race is not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the bureaucratic state apparatus; new state ministries would run against the call to smash the old state machine.

missingStatements.text: The existing state machinery should be smashed and replaced, not taken over and used.
missingStatements.rationale: Whither China? demands the old state machine be smashed utterly and replaced by Commune-type organs, a position no current statement captures.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence inferences because the ultra-left texts concern class power, the state and the army, not social or foreign policy. Chinese Trotskyists or anarchists would answer differently, e.g. on vanguard parties.
